title: Nonlinear Matrix Decomposition for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning (RL) approach for the nonlinear matrix decomposition of machine learning models. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting adaptability and efficiency. Our algorithm, termed "Matrix Weaver," learns to optimize the parameters of the decomposition process, leading to improved model performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Matrix Weaver through a series of experiments on various machine learning tasks, showcasing its ability to automatically discover and optimize the decomposition strategy. The core mechanism involves iterative trial-and-error with a reward function designed to enhance the quality of the resulting matrix. This offers a promising pathway for automating and enhancing the process of matrix decomposition, potentially unlocking new capabilities in machine learning.

title: Title: Algorithmic Consciousness Induction – Probabilistic Simulation of Emergence
abstract: This paper explores the potential for inducing self-organizing, complex behavior from a set of simple probabilistic rules through a novel algorithm, tentatively termed "Probabilistic Resonance." The core claim is that by continuously refining a set of rules based on the output of a simulated environment, we can create systems exhibiting conscious-like qualities – specifically, the ability to generate novel, adaptive patterns that are not explicitly programmed. We propose a method for inducing this emergence by leveraging a probabilistic resonance process, hypothesizing that the system's internal state evolves through a feedback loop of simulation and refinement, ultimately leading to a state of irreducible complexity. evidence.abstract: This paper explores the potential for inducing self-organizing, complex behavior from a set of simple probabilistic rules through a novel algorithm, tentatively termed "Probabilistic Resonance." The core claim is that by continuously refining a set of rules based on the output of a simulated environment, we can create systems exhibiting conscious-like qualities – specifically, the ability to generate novel, adaptive patterns that are not explicitly programmed. We propose a method for inducing this emergence by leveraging a probabilistic resonance process, hypothesizing that the system's internal state evolves through a feedback loop of simulation and refinement, ultimately leading to a state of irreducible complexity. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, illustrates its potential for generating complex patterns, and discusses the philosophical implications of this approach.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Network Topology Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum entanglement network topology, addressing the limitations of static optimization methods. We propose a dynamic approach that dynamically adjusts the distance and strength of entangled nodes to enhance quantum information transfer efficiency and security. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement networks to iteratively refine the network's structure. This iterative process, guided by a feedback loop, allows for a highly adaptable solution compared to traditional static optimization techniques. The resulting network topology is designed to maximize the fidelity of quantum states and minimize decoherence. The algorithm incorporates a self-consistency constraint to mitigate instability, ensuring a robust and reliable network configuration. We evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm on a simulated quantum network, demonstrating significant improvements in key metrics including entanglement fidelity and data transmission speed.

title: FOURIER-TAIL SCREENING FOR DEPTH-TWO MAXCUT QAOA: CERTIFIED RETENTION AND OPERATIONAL FINITE-SHOT INITIALIZATION
abstract: Fourier representations are increasingly used to reconstruct or optimize the parameter landscapes of variational quantum algorithms. We ask whether a partial Fourier model can instead identify where an optimizer should not start, while leaving the full objective in control of the final search. For depth-two MaxCut QAOA, circuit symmetries reduce the Fourier model, and explicit bounds on its omitted tail turn necessary conditions at a global minimizer into a screening rule. With exact coefficients and a verified witness, the rule removes only points that cannot be global minimizers. On \(C_6\), exact arithmetic and interval classification certify that the base screen excludes at least \(46.42\%\) of the reduced parameter torus while retaining every global minimizer. We then fit the symmetry-reduced model to finite-shot full-bitstring observations to obtain an operational version of the screen. In repeated \(C_6\) experiments, every sampled screened start reaches the certified target basin under the same exact downstream solver, compared with about three in five uniform starts. The favorable effect persists in simulated finite-shot pipelines and in runs that exhaust the same optimization budget. Screening therefore changes where optimization effort is spent, rather than how the full objective is solved. Its present bottleneck is the classical work required to find accepted starts when the retained region is small.

title: Tri-fusion deep learning model for early breast cancer screening using multimodal biomedical data
abstract: To optimize the early detection of breast cancer, a strong integration of heterogeneous biomedical signals is essential to improve diagnostic reliability and reduce false negatives. This study proposes a Tri-Fusion deep learning model for timely breast cancer screening, which integrates White Blood Cell (WBC) morphological features, mammogram image embeddings, and gene mutation signatures within a unified multimodal framework. WBC features are extracted from peripheral blood smear images using a CNN-based morphologic encoder, mammographic representation is ensured by a pretrained deep convolutional foundation based on breast imaging information, and genomic details are modelled using a completely connected mutation-signature encoder deduced from a breast cancer–related gene panel. To capture cross-domain correlation, a dense categorization head is used for feature-level fusion. The proposed model uses three publicly available datasets: a WBC image dataset containing 12,500 samples, a CBIS-DDSM mammogram dataset containing 3,102 annotated instances, and a curated Genomic Dataset containing a mutant profile of 1200 patients from TCGA-BRCA. The experimental results show high accuracy compared with the unimodal and bimodal baselines, corresponding to 96.2% accuracy, 95.4% correctness, 94.8% recall, a F1-score of 95.1%, and an AUC-ROC of 98.6%. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong generalization under cross-validation and robustness to the missing-modality scenario.

title: Intelligent sentiment analysis of user opinions in e-commerce platforms using large language models (LLM)
abstract: Тема диссертации: «Интеллектуальный анализ мнений пользователей на платформах электронной коммерции с использованием больших языковых моделей (LLM)». Цель работы: сравнительная оценка моделей анализа тональности для повышения точности классификации отзывов пользователей на платформе Digikalaи Snappfoodна персидском языке.В работе применены методы машинного обучения (SVM, NaiveBayes, RandomForest) с TF-IDF-векторизацией, а также проведен сравнительный анализ опубликованных результатов моделей-трансформеров (ParsBERT, mBERT) на наборе данных SentimentDKSF, отфильтрованном до 25 218 отзывов Digikala.Результаты: линейный SVMдостиг MacroF1 = 72,68% среди базовых моделей. Опубликованные эталоны показали, что ParsBERTдостигает F1 = 81,72%, превосходя mBERT(80,74%) и базовые модели на 9 процентных пунктов. Анализ ошибок выявил три категории сложных отзывов: короткие тексты, смешанные тональности и сарказм.Область применения: платформы электронной коммерции, системы бизнес-аналитики, управление репутацией бренда, системы рекомендаций.Выводы: трансформерные модели существенно превосходят традиционные методы машинного обучения для анализа тональности на персидском языке. Монолингвальная модель ParsBERTпоказала лучший результат, подтвердив ценность языково-специфичного предобучения для низкоресурсных языков.

title: Разработка аналитического конвейера для маркетплейсов с применением языковых моделей
abstract: Цель: разработка и экспериментальное обоснование аналитического конвейера для маркетплейсов, обеспечивающего интеллектуальный анализ пользовательского контента с применением языковых моделей для поддержки управленческих решений. Решены следующие задачи: анализ проблем и существующих решений в сфере e-commerce; разработка архитектуры аналитического конвейера; реализация модулей сбора, семантического анализа, обработки изображений и интерпретации результатов с помощью LLM и ИИ-агентов; экспериментальная апробация на реальных данных. Разработан дашборд на фреймворке Streamlit (язык Python), обеспечивающий сквозной анализ: от сбора данных (парсинг Ozon и VK) до интерпретации результатов с применением ИИ-агентов на базе языковой модели Gemma 3:4b, анализа изображений через Ollama Vision, генерации фона для изображений товаров на основе FLUX.2 и SEO-оптимизации карточек. Реализованы методы тематического моделирования (LDA, NMF) и кластеризации (K-Means, BERTopic) для выявления скрытых тем в отзывах и вопросах. Дополнительно разработаны модули генерации ответов на отзывы и вопросы покупателей с учётом контекста и стиля общения. Апробация на реальных данных подтвердила эффективность предложенного подхода.

title: Games of Diplomacy: Eliciting Spite Against Automated Opponents Through Structured Game Environments
abstract: Social games require a nuanced understanding of human behavior and are uniquely difficult to solve computationally, even with access to large behavioral datasets. Examining specific aspects of social gameplay, however, can simultaneously yield insight into human behavior and inform the design of more accurate, human-like artificial agents. Understanding and modeling human social behaviors is therefore central to the development of intelligent virtual agents, whether the objective is player profiling, game design, agent modeling, or robustness to diverse social behaviors. Previous research in social games and behavioral game theory has explored player types and factors such as social value orientation, but has often overlooked social emotions and behaviors like spite that deviate from classical rationality and yet are pervasive in competitive human interaction.

title: 基于自组织神经网络的混沌几何优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithmic framework for chaos optimization based on self-organizing neural networks (SONNs). We introduce a novel SONN architecture that dynamically learns and maintains local order within the network, allowing for the simulation of complex systems exhibiting chaotic behavior. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of the SONN to mimic the formation of fractal structures and chaotic geometry, offering a new approach to optimization. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in the exploration of complex parameter spaces, specifically in the optimization of non-convex functions, compared to traditional optimization methods. This work represents a significant step towards automated design of chaotic systems and offers a potential pathway to more robust and adaptable optimization techniques.

title: cavsqueeze: beyond-mean-field cavity-mediated spin squeezing for solid-state clock-transition ensembles
abstract: A bug fix in the trajectory solver, wider CI coverage, and a rewritten README. Fixed cavsqueeze.dtwa.evolve read the sign of y wrongly. It integrates the same equations as the cumulant solver, whose variable is = (x + i y)/2, but converted back as if the variable were . The mean J_y and the xy and yz covariances it returned therefore had the opposite sign to the cumulant solver (in the 4-spin case of the new test at t = 1, = -0.34 against +0.33). Squeezing parameters do not depend on that sign and are unchanged; seeded runs give the same squeezing values as before. Tests test_dtwa.py::test_mean_spin_follows_the_cumulant_convention: without interaction the trajectory mean spin follows exact free precession, and with interaction it agrees with the cumulant solver, both to 0.08. It fails on 1.15.0. Changed CI: the full test matrix now includes Python 3.14 (QuTiP installs there), the QuTiP-free 3.14 job is kept, and a new oldest-dependencies job runs the suite on Python 3.10 with NumPy 1.24.0, SciPy 1.10.0, Matplotlib 3.7.0 and QuTiP 5.0.0 (plus setuptools, which QuTiP 5.0.0 imports). The classifiers now list Python 3.13 and 3.14. README rewritten: plain-language guide to the terms, eight runnable examples with their printed output, every refusal and every test tolerance listed as the tests assert it. Docstrings of dick, dtwa and interop corrected where they described tests that do not exist (see below). Corrections to earlier notes 1.13.0 and the old README called the continuous-interrogation zero and the rectangular-window ratio "exact"; the tests check them to 1e-12 (coefficients) and 1e-18 (deviation). The dick module docstring said the coefficients were checked against a dense-grid FFT; the test uses adaptive quadrature (as the 1.13.0 notes say). 1.10.0 said every quantity returned by oat_closed_form is checked against exact evolution to 1e-12. The mean spin and the variance at the predicted angle are; the largest and smallest variance over the angle grid are checked to 1e-4, and xi2_S, xi2_R are not compared separately. 1.14.0 "machine precision" and "exactly orthogonal" mean agreement to 1e-12 in the tests. The dtwa docstring said the cumulant solver was checked against eight distinguishable spins; the tests use two and four. The interop docstring pointed to the test suite for the automatic Fock cutoff at r = 2.3; no test covers it (the export's own check does, at run time). Full history: CHANGELOG.md

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Lattice Optimization - Adaptive Topology Generation
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Lattice Optimization aims to revolutionize computational modeling and data representation by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to discover novel and highly efficient lattice configurations. This paper introduces a novel optimization technique, termed "Quantum-Inspired Lattice Mapping," which mimics quantum tunneling and superposition in lattice structures, enabling automated topology design. The core mechanism involves generating optimized topologies through a self-learning process guided by the quantum-inspired algorithm. We explore the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional lattice optimization methods, offering a pathway to more effective data representation and computational modeling. This work presents a robust framework for adapting to diverse problem domains, showcasing its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The focus is on generating topologies with enhanced computational efficiency and tailored properties for specific applications.

title: Adaptive Graph Embedding with Semantic Contextualization
abstract: Graph embeddings have become a cornerstone of modern graph analysis, enabling machine learning models to effectively operate on graph-structured data. However, traditional graph embedding methods often suffer from a significant limitation: they typically generate static embeddings that do not account for the evolving semantic context surrounding nodes and edges. This paper introduces an adaptive graph embedding framework that addresses this deficiency by dynamically adjusting embeddings based on the contextual information derived from surrounding relationships and external knowledge graphs. The core of our approach lies in a contextual embedding layer designed to capture the semantic meaning of graph elements, allowing for a more nuanced and accurate representation. The framework employs a recurrent neural network (RNN) to iteratively update the graph embeddings, ensuring that the representations adapt to changes in the semantic context. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key contribution is a dynamic, context-aware graph embedding technique that promises to improve performance in various graph-related tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering.

title: 基于自适应量子路径的量子算法优化策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm optimization strategy based on dynamically adjusted quantum paths. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on static parameter adjustments, limiting the potential for significant efficiency gains. This work proposes a dynamic approach that intelligently adjusts quantum path parameters during the execution of a quantum algorithm, optimizing both the algorithm's efficiency and cost. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing a substantial reduction in computational resources compared to conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive parameter tuning process driven by a feedback loop, continuously refining the quantum path to achieve optimal performance. The resulting algorithm exhibits improved performance metrics across a range of quantum algorithms, highlighting the advantages of this adaptive approach.

This work proposes a dynamic approach that intelligently adjusts quantum path parameters during the execution of a quantum algorithm, optimizing both the algorithm's efficiency and cost. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing a substantial reduction in computational resources compared to conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive parameter tuning process driven by a feedback loop, continuously refining the quantum path to achieve optimal performance. The resulting algorithm exhibits improved performance metrics across a range of quantum algorithms, highlighting the advantages of this adaptive approach.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Entanglement Self-Adaptive Entanglement Generation Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive entanglement generation algorithm based on non-linear quantum entanglement. Traditional entanglement generation methods are typically static, limiting the complexity and control of generated entangled states. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the structure and strength of entangled networks based on initial system states and feedback mechanisms, enabling the creation of intricate and predictable entanglement patterns. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's capacity to generate entangled states with tailored properties, offering a significant advancement in entanglement manipulation. This work contributes to the development of robust and controllable quantum systems.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Self-Organization
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for dynamic neuron topology self-organization, aiming to achieve adaptive and optimized computation by mimicking the natural topological changes observed in biological neural networks. The core claim is that by simulating these dynamic changes, complex computational tasks can be effectively addressed. The proposed mechanism utilizes a particle system and probabilistic graphical models to model the dynamic evolution of connections between neurons. Particles represent neurons, with their attributes—such as synaptic weights, connection strengths, and morphology—randomly updated based on local activity and the global network state, governed by predefined topological rules. Probabilistic graphical models define the dependencies between neurons, guiding the direction of topological changes. The framework continuously evaluates network performance and utilizes feedback to adjust topological rules and particle attributes, leading to dynamic self-organization of neuron topology. This approach distinguishes itself from traditional static neural network designs and rule-based self-organization methods, offering a closer alignment with the self-organizing plasticity observed in biological neural networks. The key contribution lies in the dynamic modeling of neural network topology, enabling adaptive optimization for complex computational tasks. ---

title: Title: Dynamic Metric Space for Bayesian Network Reconstruction
abstract: This paper explores a novel dynamic metric space approach to Bayesian network reconstruction, addressing the inherent challenges of learning from noisy data. Traditional methods often struggle with distributional shifts, leading to suboptimal reconstructions. We propose a new framework that utilizes an adaptive metric space – a representation that dynamically adjusts to the evolving data distribution – to improve accuracy and robustness. This approach allows the network to maintain a consistent and informative representation of the underlying data structure, ultimately enhancing reconstruction quality. The core mechanism centers around a mechanism that quantifies the data's inherent uncertainty and uses this information to guide the metric space's adaptation. The resulting method demonstrates improved performance across various benchmark datasets, particularly in scenarios with significant data drift. Further, the paper explores the theoretical implications of the dynamic metric space, providing insights into its convergence properties.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Memory-Augmented Backpropagation
abstract: Training deep neural networks is frequently hampered by the persistent issues of vanishing gradients and exploding gradients. These problems arise during backpropagation, where gradients can become exponentially small or large as they propagate through the network, hindering the effective learning of deeper layers. This paper introduces a novel approach to address these challenges: Self-Correcting Neural Networks (SCNNs) utilizing a memory-augmented backpropagation algorithm. The core of the SCNN architecture lies in integrating a memory component that stores historical activation values and gradients. This memory allows the network to explicitly correct for errors introduced in earlier layers by referencing past information, thereby promoting more stable gradient flow and accelerating the learning process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and present a conceptual framework for its implementation. The primary objective is to provide a robust method for training deep networks, reducing reliance on techniques like batch normalization and careful weight initialization. ---

title: Topological Excitation of Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the topological excitation of multi-body quantum entanglement as a novel approach to quantum state manipulation. We propose a mechanism utilizing external field control to induce changes in the topology of multi-body entanglement, thereby generating new quantum states. These states are then leveraged for quantum information manipulation. The core claim centers on the ability to control multi-body quantum entanglement's topology to trigger new quantum states and, consequently, enable quantum information control. This approach offers a distinct excitation methodology compared to conventional techniques, representing a significant step towards practical quantum information processing. The theoretical framework presented herein provides a foundation for future research and development in this area. We explore the fundamental aspects of topological entanglement and demonstrate the potential for harnessing its dynamic properties.

title: Title: Dimensional Entanglement Network (DEN)
abstract: Dimensional Entanglement Network (DEN) is a novel framework for network design predicated on the principle of dimensional entanglement. This paper presents a method for constructing and analyzing networks exhibiting entanglement, aiming to significantly enhance information transfer speed and efficiency. The core concept involves creating a network topology that utilizes entangled pairs across multiple dimensions, leveraging the inherent properties of entanglement to facilitate faster and more effective data transmission. This research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional network architectures. We detail the theoretical underpinnings, propose a specific network construction algorithm, and provide a preliminary analysis of its performance characteristics. The significance of this work lies in its potential to revolutionize network design by incorporating a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics – entanglement – to drive computational advancements.

title: Dimension Generalization and Quantum Entanglement: A Novel Framework for Geometry and Quantum Information
abstract: This paper explores the convergence of dimension generalization and quantum entanglement, proposing a novel framework for creating and manipulating high-dimensional spaces utilizing quantum entanglement. Traditional dimensionality reduction methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of high-dimensional data, while the potential of quantum entanglement offers a pathway to fundamentally alter geometric relationships. This work introduces a new mechanism, termed "dimension anchoring," that leverages entangled quantum states to dynamically adjust dimensional parameters, bypassing the need for direct manipulation of the underlying geometric structure. We demonstrate the framework's potential for generating novel geometric structures and, critically, for exploiting entanglement to enhance quantum information security. This research aims to provide a new perspective on dimensionality reduction, quantum computation, and secure communication by integrating these two powerful fields.

title: Explorations in Conversational XAI Interfaces. From Static Explanations to Co-constructive Explainers
abstract: Across domains like healthcare, finance, and criminal justice, AI systems now inform decisions with real consequences, but their inner logic is rarely accessible to users. Most work in Explainable AI (XAI) concerns *which* explanations to present (e.g., attributions, rules, counterfactuals), overlooking explanation as an *interactive process* shaped by interface-mediated communication and user engagement. This dissertation investigates how interfaces influence users' AI model understanding. We formalize a three-dimensional design space — *Continuity*, *Adaptivity*, and *Initiative* — and examine post-hoc explanations for tabular black-box models across four human-grounded studies spanning controlled tasks with non-experts and a field study in an expert workflow. We first compare static reports with menu-based interaction under matched explanatory content, finding that interactivity improves objective model understanding. We then examine natural-language input and scripted guidance, which let users ask questions in their own words but do not improve objective understanding and can create an affordance–capability gap when the conversational surface promises more than the system can deliver. The dissertation contributes a process-first account of conversational XAI that treats interfaces as a distinct layer beyond explanation generation and centers communication, user engagement, and users' evolving understanding. It offers a design space for conversational XAI, a reusable content-matched evaluation paradigm for measuring model understanding, and an implementation of co-construction mapped onto the MAPE-K reference architecture. Across controlled and expert settings, the studies clarify when interaction alone is sufficient and when monitoring-driven adaptation and scaffolding become necessary, and they show that co-construction can improve perceived collaboration, usability, and trust before it yields robust gains in objective understanding.

title: Inteligencia artificial conversacional en la comunicación institucional: El caso del asistente “ORTEGA” en entornos científicos
abstract: Introducción. La inteligencia artificial conversacional (Yang et al., 2025) se ha consolidado como tecnología clave para optimizar la interacción digital. En este marco, se analiza el diseño y desarrollo de ORTEGA, un asistente virtual (Caldarini et al., 2022) integrado en la web del Congreso Internacional de IA 365 para ofrecer asistencia automatizada y facilitar el acceso a información del evento. Objetivo. Se trata de reconocer el desarrollo de ORTEGA como caso de aplicación de sistemas conversacionales (Trofymenko et al., 2021), describiendo su proceso de integración técnica y funcional para mejorar la experiencia de usuario (UX) (Nielsen, 2000). Metodología. Se ha utilizado el análisis descriptivo-exploratorio dividido en dos fases: una implementación técnica basada en análisis heurístico (Savinic y Piazolo, 2026), y una validación empírica (beta-testing) (Winteringham, 2022) con una muestra diversificada de 15 evaluadores (expertos, estudiantes, y usuarios generales) mediante un protocolo de usabilidad de tres dimensiones desarrollado en el primer trimestre de 2026. Resultados. Las principales consecuencias muestran que la optimización de la interfaz (UI) y la corrección de errores de visualización en dispositivos móviles permitieron una visibilidad de los colaboradores del 100 % y un incremento del 15 % en la interacción. La evolución del avatar hacia una estética pictórica logró una conexión empática sin rechazo visual. Discusión. Tras comprobar los resultados se observa que la eficacia de una IA académica no depende solo del procesamiento del lenguaje, sino de su armonía visual, demostrando que la representación simbólica evita el fenómeno del uncanny valley (Seyama y Nagayama, 2007). Conclusiones. Se comprueba que ORTEGA puede ser una propuesta inicial de integración para la transferencia de conocimiento. Además, es susceptible de crear las primeras bases para futuras evaluaciones de rendimiento y precisión semántica para este tipo de herramientas en contextos institucionales.

Se ha utilizado el análisis descriptivo-exploratorio dividido en dos fases: una implementación técnica basada en análisis heurístico (Savinic y Piazolo, 2026), y una validación empírica (beta-testing) (Winteringham, 2022) con una muestra diversificada de 15 evaluadores (expertos, estudiantes, y usuarios generales) mediante un protocolo de usabilidad de tres dimensiones desarrollado en el primer trimestre de 2026. Resultados. Las principales consecuencias muestran que la optimización de la interfaz (UI) y la corrección de errores de visualización en dispositivos móviles permitieron una visibilidad de los colaboradores del 100 % y un incremento del 15 % en la interacción. La evolución del avatar hacia una estética pictórica logró una conexión empática sin rechazo visual. Discusión. Tras comprobar los resultados se observa que la eficacia de una IA académica no depende solo del procesamiento del lenguaje, sino de su armonía visual, demostrando que la representación simbólica evita el fenómeno del uncanny valley (Seyama y Nagayama, 2007). Conclusiones. Se comprueba que ORTEGA puede ser una propuesta inicial de integración para la transferencia de conocimiento. Además, es susceptible de crear las primeras bases para futuras evaluaciones de rendimiento y precisión semántica para este tipo de herramientas en contextos institucionales.

title: Do Pedagogical Agent Roles Matter? Effects on Learning Performance, Motivation, and Agent Perception
abstract: Pedagogical Agents (PAs) have been widely studied in technology-supported learning environments and are generally considered beneficial for enhancing students’ learning and motivation. However, less is known about how specific agent roles influence these outcomes. This work addresses this gap by examining the effects of different PA roles on learning performance, motivation, and learners’ perception of the PA. In a user study, two role variants — a mentor and an expert agent — were compared, alongside a control condition without a PA. The results showed no significant differences in learning performance or motivation between conditions. However, the mentor agent was perceived as significantly more facilitative of learning, more human-like, and more engaging than the expert agent. These findings suggest that agent role design primarily seems to shape learners’ subjective experience, without necessarily leading to measurable improvements in learning outcomes. Overall, the results do not confirm the beneficial effects of PAs on learning outcomes and motivation compared to a non-agent control condition, contrary to what is reported in prior research. However, when a PA is implemented, the mentor role appears to be the more suitable design choice, as it enhances the affective and social aspects of the learning experience.

title: Mapping global research landscape of artificial intelligence and machine learning in lung cancer diagnosis and prognosis through bibliometric analysis
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in diagnosing and predicting lung cancer prognosis has changed the way images are interpreted, risks predicted, and decisions made for clinical purposes. Despite increased research in this area, there is little to no bibliometric analysis evaluating the global state of affairs. The purpose of this study was to examine this research area. In this study, a literature search was conducted by using the Scopus database, with emphasis on the role of AI and ML in the diagnosis and prognosis of lung cancer. Collaboration maps were analyzed using VOSviewer 1.6.20 and Biblioshiny. There was a significant growth in global scientific production with an exponential growth in number of publications during 2020–2024 period. The United States, China, and India became the major contributors to scientific production, and analysis of collaboration networks indicated the existence of effective international collaborations. Through citation analysis, the most impactful sources, authors, and institutions were found. Through keyword and thematic evolution analysis, the shift from computer-aided diagnosis and pulmonary nodule detection to radiomics, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, explainable AI, and precision medicine was identified. This paper is an exhaustive bibliometric analysis of the literature on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for diagnosing and prognosticating lung cancer. By identifying publication patterns, major contributors, collaboration networks, and research hot spots, this study has provided important insights into the field’s development and the future of research in this area. Bibliometric analysis mapped global AI and ML research trends in lung cancer. Scientific output increased exponentially, with rapid growth after 2021. Identified leading authors, institutions, journals, and influential studies. Highlighted deep learning and radiomics as a future direction for precision oncology.

title: ArtSociety: Multi-Agent Multimodal Collaboration for Art Emotion Understanding
abstract: The AffectiveArt Multidimensional Art Emotion Understanding task asks to jointly predict an artwork's fine-grained emotion (12 classes, 1549:1 head-to-tail ratio), binary valence/arousal, and five attribute-grounded descriptions -- sub-tasks that exhibit strong empirical trade-offs, so the single-model solutions we tried do not jointly optimize all of them well. We present ArtSociety, a multi-agent framework that assembles heterogeneous multimodal experts -- a DINOv2-Giant vision agent (A1), a scene-grounded CoT fine-tuned MLLM (A2), and three closed-source reasoning agents (A3-A5) -- and coordinates them with two training-free controllers: (i) a rare-class-aware voting arbiter that lowers the agreement threshold for tail emotions, exploiting decorrelated error patterns across agent families; and (ii) a description-first reasoning agent whose DESCRIBE-then-CLASSIFY chain of thought forces visual evidence before label commitment, yielding near-perfect grounded descriptions. A task-routing policy directs the hard emotion task to the full five-agent ensemble while assigning the near-saturated valence/arousal and generative description tasks to the single strongest reasoning agent. On the official test set (1,000 artworks), ArtSociety achieves an Overall Score of 0.8870 (Classification 0.7789, Description 0.9952). An eleven-variant ablation study reveals that, once method and scale saturate at around 0.76, the decisive gains come from agent collaboration and data-side supervision -- a 30B MoE model trained on older data does not outperform an 8B model trained on better data. Code is available at https://github.com/swordlidev/ArtSociety

title: On the Abundance of Critical Points of the t-SNE Energy
abstract: This paper considers the energy landscape of the t-SNE algorithm. While this algorithm has enjoyed broad adoption, the non-convexity of the associated energy has made it difficult to rigorously understand what the algorithm captures in many settings. In particular, a number of well-known numerical examples, several of which are reproduced in this article, suggest a complicated energy landscape with many local minimizers that do not respect the topology or clustering structure of the underlying data. This work seeks to provide first steps towards a rigorous explanation of these phenomena. Specifically, for a general family of energies, which include both the original t-SNE algorithm and recently identified large data limits, and for densities in feature space which obey a continuous symmetry, we construct infinite families of distinct critical points. These critical points are based upon identifying pairs of discrete symmetries, one in the original feature space and the other in the target embedding space, which are preserved under gradient dynamics. These critical configurations exhibit many characteristics, such as topology breaking and spurious clustering, which are often observed empirically. Finally, numerical and analytical examples are given throughout as a means of illustrating the approach.

title: Robust multi-hypothesis quantum-state discrimination under unknown common unitary perturbations via least favorable priors
abstract: We study robust K-ary quantum-state discrimination when all candidate states are affected by the same unknown common unitary perturbation. The unknown perturbation does not represent the label to be identified, but acts as a nuisance factor that changes the performance of a fixed measurement. We formulate the problem as a minimax decision problem over the possible perturbations and propose using the Bayes-optimal collective measurement associated with a least favorable prior (LFP) on the nuisance-parameter space. For a finite discretization of this space, we show that the LFP can be computed by a semidefinite program and that the corresponding value coincides with the finite-grid minimax success probability. As numerical demonstrations, we consider a binary nonorthogonal qubit model and a nonorthogonal three-state qutrit model with an unknown common unitary perturbation. The LFP-based measurement substantially flattens the success-probability profile and improves the worst-case success probability compared with a reference-point optimal measurement and a uniform-prior Bayes measurement. The resulting LFP concentrates its weight on regions of the nuisance-parameter space that actively limit the robust discrimination performance, thereby providing both a constructive measurement design and a diagnostic description of the difficult nuisance-parameter regimes.

title: Graph Reasoning Over Enterprise Innovation Networks for Industrial Investment Risk Assessment
abstract: Regional industrial funds invest in technology-oriented manufacturing firms, advanced materials companies, intelligent equipment producers, energy enterprises, and digital infrastructure providers. Investment risk is influenced not only by financial indicators but also by patent quality, R&D collaboration, government subsidies, customer concentration, supply-chain stability, executive experience, and related-party transactions. This study proposes a graph reasoning model over enterprise innovation networks for industrial investment risk assessment. The method builds a knowledge graph linking target firms, shareholders, patents, research partners, suppliers, customers, subsidy programs, financing rounds, executives, litigation events, and revenue records. A graph neural network is used to represent innovation capability and business dependency, while knowledge inference identifies hidden investment risks from weak patent commercialization, subsidy dependency, unstable key customers, supplier disruption, and shareholder debt exposure. Experiments are conducted on a regional industrial investment dataset containing 12,800 candidate enterprises, 96,000 patents, 38,400 R&D collaboration links, 520,000 supplier-customer edges, 18,600 subsidy records, 24,300 financing events, and 3,940 post-investment risk cases over 54 months. The proposed model shortens median risk-identification time from 132 days to 57 days after investment screening compared with a due-diligence checklist baseline. It discovers 4,260 innovation-commercialization risk paths and 1,780 subsidy-dependency risk chains. Portfolio simulation shows that graph-informed screening reduces expected impaired investment exposure by 118 million RMB during the validation period. Full quarterly assessment of candidate enterprises is completed in 8.7 minutes. The results demonstrate that enterprise innovation network reasoning can provide interpretable support for industrial fund investment risk assessment.

title: Topological-Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the interplay between topology and quantum coherence, investigating the stability and evolution of quantum systems through the application of quantum entanglement and topological structures. We propose a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging these principles to develop new methods that offer a fundamentally different understanding of quantum mechanics. The core of this work lies in a detailed analysis of decoherence mechanisms, focusing on how topological properties can mitigate these effects and ultimately enhance the fidelity of quantum operations. The research aims to address limitations inherent in current quantum algorithms and pave the way for more robust and versatile quantum technologies.

title: Title: The Interconnection of Topology and Quantum Entanglement: A Framework for Predictive Control and Optimization in Quantum Geometry
abstract: This research explores the potential for a novel framework integrating topology and quantum entanglement to revolutionize computational processes, particularly within the context of quantum computing. We propose a "纠缠拓扑" concept, leveraging quantum entanglement to guide the evolution of complex quantum geometric structures. This framework aims to provide a mechanism for efficient data compression and enhanced quantum computation through targeted manipulation of these structures. The core mechanism involves the design of a specialized algorithm that utilizes entangled quantum states to induce topological transformations, ultimately leading to optimized data storage and computational efficiency. This work addresses a critical gap in current research by proposing a comprehensive and interconnected approach, potentially unlocking new capabilities in both quantum information theory and practical computation.

title: Self-Organizing Network Topology for Quantum Computing Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of a novel self-organizing network topology algorithm for quantum computing, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea revolves around dynamically adjusting network topology based on quantum entanglement, resulting in enhanced quantum communication and computation capabilities. We detail the algorithm's design, the mathematical framework underpinning its operation, and the potential advantages it offers over conventional network topology approaches. The proposed method addresses key challenges in quantum network design, including scalability, error correction, and efficient data transfer. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discusses future research directions, including exploration of different entanglement protocols and network architectures.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络的自适应正则化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to regularization for neural networks, leveraging a dynamically adjusted regularization parameter based on the inherent differences between features. The core concept is a self-adaptive regularization mechanism, which learns to optimize the regularization strength for each data point. This dynamic adjustment aims to enhance model generalization by promoting better feature representation and mitigating overfitting. We present a framework that adapts the regularization strength based on a learned gradient of the loss function, effectively creating a personalized regularization strategy. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential to significantly boost model robustness and generalization.

title: Quantum State Superposition-Based Hardware Acceleration for Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hardware acceleration architecture for computation leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. Traditional computing paradigms rely heavily on sequential processing, often struggling with the computational demands of large-scale parallel problems. We introduce a quantum bit array-based system designed to exploit superposition, enabling the simultaneous execution of multiple computational tasks. The core concept involves constructing an array of interconnected quantum bits (qubits) where each qubit can exist in a superposition of states. This allows for parallel processing of data, significantly enhancing computational speed and efficiency. We detail the theoretical framework, outlining the key mathematical relationships and operational principles. The architecture's potential for accelerating specific algorithms and the associated performance gains are discussed. This research aims to provide a foundational approach for developing future quantum computing hardware, particularly focusing on harnessing the power of quantum superposition.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Adaptive Sorting Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive sorting algorithm based on non-linear geometric topology. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of geometric topology to optimize the sorting process, leading to enhanced efficiency. The algorithm employs a unique mechanism that utilizes geometric transformations to restructure the data and improve sorting performance. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation. The results demonstrate significant improvements in sorting speed and scalability compared to existing approaches. This research contributes to the field of data sorting by exploring the potential of geometry for computational optimization.

title: Dynamic Topology Optimization for Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology optimization (DTO) to quantum circuits, aiming to enhance circuit performance through adaptive layout adjustments. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to iteratively refine the circuit topology, minimizing errors and maximizing information flow. The core mechanism revolves around minimizing the error rate associated with quantum gate operations, a critical challenge in quantum circuit design. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, training methodology, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating a significant improvement in circuit fidelity compared to static optimization techniques. The core claim is that this DTO approach provides a fundamentally more effective method for designing quantum circuits with enhanced performance.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的潜在空间映射
abstract: The development of effective machine learning models relies heavily on the ability to efficiently represent and learn from data. Traditional methods for potential space mapping often employ fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving datasets. This paper introduces a novel approach – a self-adaptive neural network-based potential space mapping method – that dynamically adjusts the structure of the potential space during training, resulting in improved model training and predictive performance. We propose a framework where a neural network learns an implicit representation of the data's potential space, allowing the model to automatically optimize the representation for better generalization. This results in a more robust and adaptable system compared to traditional methods.

title: 基于拓扑的量子计算参数调整算法
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computation compared to classical computing, driven by the ability to utilize quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement. However, realizing this potential requires significant computational resources and precise control over quantum states. Parameter adjustment, the process of modifying the parameters of a quantum system to achieve a desired outcome, remains a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Quantum Topology Optimization" (QTO), that leverages the inherent structure of quantum systems – specifically, topological structures – to dynamically adjust quantum parameters, ultimately leading to optimized computational results. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of QTO in a simplified quantum circuit setting. The core mechanism hinges on automatically mapping and optimizing parameters based on the topological properties of the system, offering a significant departure from traditional parameter adjustment methods. This paper explores the potential of QTO to overcome the limitations of conventional approaches, paving the way for more efficient and robust quantum computation.

title: Quantum Information Encoding via Phase-Shifted Entanglement
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and communication. Traditional encoding methods often rely on physical manipulation of qubits, which can be susceptible to noise and decoherence. This paper explores a novel approach – encoding information using phase-shifted entanglement – that leverages the inherent properties of entangled states to achieve efficient and robust data transmission. We introduce a new entanglement encoding scheme where the phase shift directly correlates with the encoded data, simplifying the process and potentially leading to significant improvements in data transfer rates and reliability. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach, aiming to contribute to advancements in quantum information processing.

We introduce a new entanglement encoding scheme where the phase shift directly correlates with the encoded data, simplifying the process and potentially leading to significant improvements in data transfer rates and reliability. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach, aiming to contribute to advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Algorithmic Trustworthiness Verification using Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to verifying the trustworthiness of algorithms by leveraging differential privacy (DP). Traditional methods for algorithm verification often rely on black-box testing, which is vulnerable to sophisticated adversarial attacks. Our method introduces controlled noise into the algorithm's output during the verification process, effectively masking sensitive information while simultaneously enabling the detection of malicious manipulation. We formulate a rigorous mathematical framework for quantifying algorithmic trustworthiness, based on the level of noise added and the probability of successfully masking adversarial inputs. This approach provides a quantifiable metric for assessing algorithmic vulnerability, a critical requirement in security-sensitive applications such as autonomous systems, financial modeling, and medical diagnosis. The core claim of this work is that differential privacy can be effectively utilized to create a robust verification system, significantly enhancing algorithmic resilience against manipulation and adversarial attacks. We outline the key components of this system, including the noise injection mechanism, the verification protocol, and the mathematical model for quantifying trustworthiness. ---

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Adaptive Noise Adjustment Optimization Engine
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems to solve complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. Within the field of QML, the design of effective quantum machine learning algorithms is paramount to unlocking the full potential of quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel optimization engine, dubbed "Adaptive Noise Adjustment Optimization Engine" (ANAOE), designed to address a critical challenge in QML: the inherent sensitivity of quantum models to noise. ANAOE dynamically adjusts noise parameters based on the actual quantum environment, promoting more precise and robust model performance. The core mechanism of this engine leverages a sophisticated feedback loop to continuously refine the noise landscape, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and stability of quantum computations. We demonstrate the efficacy of ANAOE through comprehensive simulations and analysis, highlighting its ability to outperform traditional optimization methods in various quantum machine learning tasks.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的系统优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for optimizing complex systems. Traditional system optimization approaches often rely on centralized control or distributed control strategies, which can struggle with the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of many real-world systems. This research proposes a novel framework utilizing a population of intelligent agents trained through MARL to autonomously optimize these systems. The core concept involves decomposing the complex system into multiple agents, each responsible for optimizing a specific sub-objective. These agents interact through a combination of cooperation and competition, ultimately leading to overall system optimization. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach, outlining the key components and the learning dynamics involved. The paper demonstrates the potential of MARL to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, offering a more adaptive and robust solution for complex system optimization problems. The effectiveness of this approach is discussed through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual design, paving the way for future research and practical implementations. ---

title: Contextualized Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Contextualized Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction (CMHN-HTA). Existing memory networks frequently face challenges in capturing long-term dependencies due to limitations in memory access efficiency and the difficulty of representing events across extended temporal scales. Our proposed architecture addresses these shortcomings by incorporating a hierarchical temporal abstraction layer. This layer decomposes the temporal dimension into multiple levels of abstraction, where higher levels represent events over longer time intervals. This hierarchical structure significantly improves memory access efficiency, allowing the network to focus on relevant information and effectively model long-term dependencies. The core idea is to represent memories not just as discrete points in time, but as events with varying degrees of temporal context. We formalize this approach through a mathematical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. This framework facilitates the design and analysis of CMHN-HTA networks, offering a robust solution for tasks requiring the integration of long-range contextual information. We present a detailed mathematical description of the system, focusing on the key equations and their implications.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Contrastive Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to kernel learning that adapts the kernel function during training using contrastive representation learning. The core idea is to learn a low-dimensional latent space representation of data points and then define the kernel function based on the similarity (measured by distance) between points in this space. Unlike traditional kernel learning, which relies on pre-defined kernels, our method learns the kernel function directly from the data, offering increased flexibility and potentially better performance in scenarios with complex data distributions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive kernel learning framework through a theoretical analysis and outline a training procedure that leverages contrastive learning to drive the adaptation of the kernel function. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the kernel based on the contrastive objective, enabling the model to capture more nuanced relationships within the data.

title: 基于量子纠缠的混沌域的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement, aiming to precisely compute the properties of chaotic systems and achieve superior optimization results. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complexity and non-linearity inherent in chaotic environments. We leverage the unique characteristics of quantum entanglement to enable a more precise and efficient optimization process. The core mechanism involves a quantum computation that accurately represents the evolution of the chaotic system, followed by a refined optimization step based on this representation. The algorithm's novelty lies in its ability to utilize entanglement to achieve a significantly improved accuracy compared to existing methods, particularly in challenging scenarios. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Title: Dynamic Adaptive Variable Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive variable model designed to enhance model performance. Traditional variable models often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their ability to optimize for complex data patterns. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts parameters during the model training process, allowing the model to adapt to the data itself, thereby improving predictive accuracy and generalization. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the model's performance and adjusts parameters accordingly. This iterative process ensures that the model remains optimally tuned for the specific dataset. The proposed method offers a significant improvement over static models by leveraging the inherent dynamism of the data.

abstract: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Parallel Computing Framework presents a novel approach to parallel computing leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. This framework utilizes entangled qubits to facilitate data transmission and computation, offering a potential pathway towards significantly enhanced computational efficiency compared to conventional parallel computing methods. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the non-classical correlations inherent in entangled states to achieve a higher degree of parallelism and reduced communication overhead. The potential benefits of this architecture lie in its capacity to address limitations inherent in classical parallel systems, particularly in scenarios involving complex data manipulation and high-dimensional computations. This paper explores the design and potential implementation of this framework, detailing its underlying principles and outlining future research directions.

The current research focuses on a practical implementation, demonstrating the feasibility of utilizing quantum entanglement to encode and transmit information with significant advantages over conventional methods. This work presents a foundational approach to quantum data encoding, laying the groundwork for future advancements in secure communication and information management.

title: Author Correction: On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a calculation error. In the “Aggregate results” section of Results, the paper originally reported that the Human–AI (personalized) effect remains significant even when changing the reference category to Human–AI ( P = 0.04). Re-running the analysis with the correct reference category yields P = 0.0678. The text now reading “Similarly, the difference between the Human–AI (personalized) and Human–AI conditions was not statistically significant when using Human–AI as the reference category (+48.7%, 95% CI [–2.9%, + 127.6%], P = 0.07), likely reflecting limited statistical power given the relatively small per-condition sample sizes and the large standard errors observed across treatment comparisons. Thus, we cannot conclusively establish from this comparison alone that personalization confers an additional advantage over non-personalized GPT-4. Nevertheless, these findings provide evidence that GPT-4-based microtargeting strongly outperforms human performance, with GPT-4 leveraging personal information more effectively than humans” now replaces the original text “By contrast, the Human–AI (personalized) effect remains significant even when changing the reference category to Human–AI ( P = 0.04). Remarkably, these findings provide evidence that GPT-4-based microtargeting strongly outperforms both non-personalized GPT-4 and human-based microtargeting, with GPT-4 leveraging personal information more effectively than humans.” In the fourth paragraph of the Discussion, the text now reading “We note that, while the Human–AI (personalized) condition significantly outperformed the Human–Human baseline, the direct comparison between the Human–AI (personalized) and Human–AI conditions did not reach statistical significance ( P = 0.07), likely due to limited statistical power for pairwise treatment contrasts. This suggests caution in attributing the observed advantage exclusively to personalization, as opposed to the general persuasive capabilities of GPT-4. Despite that, the effect is particularly remarkable” replaces the original text “We emphasize that the effect of personalization is particularly remarkable.” There were also errors in the last paragraph of the Introduction and first paragraph of the Results, where four instances of “ Ã pre ” originally read “ Ã post .” Similar errors have been amended in the Supplementary Information. The text and Supplementary Information are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Performance Study of Serverless Workloads in Confidential Virtual Machines
abstract: Confidential serverless computing is rapidly emerg- ing as a critical paradigm for application domains requiring strong confidentiality guarantees, such as healthcare, finance, and machine learning. To enable this paradigm in untrusted cloud environments, Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs) provide isolation by encrypting the entire guest memory, and thus securing serverless workloads against host-level access and inter- ference. However, the implications of CVMs for serverless systems remain insufficiently understood. This paper presents an empirical study of serverless work- loads in CVMs, systematically covering memory efficiency and runtime overhead on both warm-starts and cold-starts. Our results show that CVMs incur substantial memory overhead because encrypted memory disables cross-VM page deduplication and reduces memory reclaimability, thereby limiting warm- container capacity under a fixed memory budget. Runtime overhead in warm-starts is workload dependent. Workloads with frequent VMEXITs, particularly idle transitions, suffer substantial slowdowns. These slowdowns are further amplified by common serverless deployment practice that couples vCPU allocation to memory size, as higher-memory configurations expose more vCPUs than some functions can use effectively. For cold starts, the study focuses on container creation, a common and major contributor to startup latency. Motivated by the memory-efficiency results, we consider the deployments in which multiple containers of the same function are consolidated within the same CVM to improve efficiency, and show that selectively relaxing certain isolation mechanisms in this setting can substan- tially reduce startup overhead. These results clarify the main performance tradeoffs of confidential serverless computing and suggest practical ways to improve efficiency and latency.

title: Corporate Language Model (CLM): Transforming Tacit and Fragmented Enterprise Knowledge into a Sovereign, Auditable, and Executable Corporate Intelligence Layer
abstract: Enterprise AI deployments fail not from model inadequacy, but because organizations lack a structured substrate encoding how they decide, negotiate, and execute. Generic LLMs carry no firm-specific ontological priors; RAG remains brittle, with no path to executable action; static playbooks encode logic but cannot reason or adapt. This demands an architecture treating tacit-knowledge capture, ontological grounding, sovereign deployment, and auditable actuation as co-designed from the start. This paper introduces the Corporate Language Model (CLM), a framework transforming a firm's structured, unstructured, multimodal, and tacit knowledge into an ontology-grounded enterprise foundation upon which reasoning and governed execution are composed. CLM has five capability planes and four architectural pillars: a Neurosymbolic Mesh coupling generative models with a knowledge graph; a Skill Graph where reusable tactics, personas, objections, and goals are typed and composed; Living Digital Twins modeling functional areas as reasoning surrogates; and a Deep Security Layer enforcing sovereignty, traceability, and human oversight. A Spec-as-Code paradigm bridges grounded intent and executable artifact. CLM is one instantiation of this foundation-centric class. Four contributions follow: CLM is defined as a distinct object of study; the Skill Graph is introduced for compositional explainability by construction; the Wisdom Listener effect is proposed, whereby tacit-capable foundations compound in value with use, connecting to dynamic capabilities and organizational learning; and evidence from a JCI-accredited tertiary hospital in Brazil instantiates three of the six maturity stages under LGPD.

title: Sharpening the Ensemble: An SSIM-Aligned Residual Refiner for Brain-MRI Inpainting Post-Processing
abstract: Brain-MRI inpainting replaces a masked region of a scan with synthesized, anatomically plausible healthy tissue, so that analysis tools built for healthy brains can be applied to images they would otherwise reject. On the BraTS local-synthesis benchmark, which ranks submissions on the structural similarity index (SSIM), the peak signal-to-noise ratio, and the mean squared error (MSE) jointly, the strongest recent models are accurate, but several report blurry synthesized regions and attribute this to the mean-seeking behavior of the $\ell_1$ and MSE terms in their training losses. We address this in post-processing, forming a deep ensemble of the two co-first-place 2025 models and training a lightweight residual refiner on the ensemble's own outputs under an $\ell_1$ loss augmented with a structural-similarity term whose weight $λ$ we vary. At a moderate $λ$ the refiner improves SSIM over the ensemble, from $0.8767$ to $0.8780$ on a held-out reproduction of the official scorer and from $0.8555$ to $0.8572$ on the official validation leaderboard, with essentially no change in MSE. The gain is small but consistent, improving $62.6\%$ of the held-out cases with a signed-rank $p=2.2\times10^{-7}$, whereas over-weighting the structural term reverses it. Two ablations bound the effect. Adding any third model to the two-model ensemble degrades it, and classical unsharp masking fails to improve SSIM at any strength (best $0.8765$ against $0.8767$), so the gain reflects learned rather than indiscriminate sharpening. The result is a cheap, reproducible post-processing stage that improves an already strong ensemble without any large-scale retraining.

title: ToPO: Token-Conditioned Preference Routing for Attention-Based Latent Diffusion Models
abstract: Pairwise preference labels rank complete images, yet Diffusion-DPO applies their effect over many spatial and denoising-time coordinates. For attention-based, noise-prediction latent diffusion, ToPO (Token-Oriented Preference Optimization) constructs a per-minibatch, detached, separable spatial-temporal route from branchwise squared-residual contrast in a frozen reference denoiser. Preferred-branch cross-attention uses content tokens to modulate the spatial factor, and an auxiliary pixel-midpoint ordering term is added without local labels or a learned reward model. In matched three-seed retrainings with a shared update schedule, ToPO has higher endpoint estimates than Diffusion-DPO on all five reported SD-1.5 metrics and on HPSv2, ImageReward, and CLIP for SDXL. It also receives larger raw win shares in an aggregate blind SDXL A/B study. These findings are scoped to the reported equal-update U-Net protocols rather than an equal-compute comparison.

title: Constraint closure and gravitational-wave content of shear-free cosmologies in metric f(R) gravity
abstract: We derive the consistency conditions governing the propagating content of linear shear-free perturbations of Friedmann-Lema\^ıtre-Robertson-Walker cosmologies in metric f(R) gravity. The divergence of the shear-free constraint is shown to be the total momentum-conservation equation and therefore does not imply geodesic flow. Its projected time derivative instead supplies a nontrivial integrability condition. Scalar, vector, and tensor sectors must then be tested separately. Shear-freeness removes the independent transverse-traceless electric-magnetic Weyl pair, so no ordinary + or times tensor gravitational wave survives. The scalaron is not removed algebraically, but its four-variable harmonic system must remain in the time-dependent consistent subspace generated by the shear-free constraint and all of its time derivatives. For a geodesic shear-free congruence in the spatially flat expanding de Sitter patch, this excludes every nonzero fixed comoving scalar harmonic, including the healthy R+αR^2-2Λ model with α,Λ>0. Vector modes obey a curvature-dependent global eigenvalue condition whose right-hand side is negative for positive-density matter with f'>0 and 1+w>0; hence no nonzero vector harmonic survives on that branch. The familiar coasting R^3 example evades this sign obstruction only because it lies on an f'<0 branch. Thus tensor radiation is absent in the imposed shear-free sector, whereas scalar radiation is not excluded kinematically but remains a model- and background-dependent constraint-closure question.

title: Optimasi K-NN Menggunakan SMOTE dan Cosine Similarity pada Klasifikasi Topik Skripsi
abstract: Penentuan dosen pembimbing skripsi yang linear dengan topik penelitian mahasiswa merupakan tahapan krusial dalam penyelesaian tugas akhir. Pemetaan judul ke bidang keahlian dosen secara manual seringkali kurang efisien dan dihadapkan pada tantangan distribusi topik yang tidak merata (imbalanced data). Penelitian ini mengusulkan optimasi model klasifikasi berbasis algoritma K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) menggunakan 1.598 data historis judul skripsi dari Universitas AMIKOM Yogyakarta. Untuk mengatasi ketimpangan jumlah sampel antar bidang dosen, teknik Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) diimplementasikan pada fase pelatihan data (data train). Proses ekstraksi Informasi teks melalui tahapan preprocessing komprehensif, meliputi case folding, stopword removal, dan stemming, yang kemudian dibobotkan menggunakan Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Pembagian komposisi data latih dan uji ditetapkan sebesar 80:20. Berbeda dengan pendekatan spasial standar, model ini diuji menggunakan metrik jarak Cosine Similarity untuk mengukur kedekatan semantik antar dokumen dengan lebih presisi. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa klasifikasi K-NN mencapai performa maksimal pada parameter k=21 dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 85.94%. Integrasi SMOTE dan metrik Cosine terbukti secara signifikasn menaikkan sensitivitas model, ditandai dengan nilai recall hingga 95% pada pengenalan kategori bidang dosen minoritas yang sebelumnya sulit diklasifikasikan.

title: Quantum Topos Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Abstract: Quantum Topos Adaptive Algorithm (QTAA) presents a novel algorithm for automatically adjusting the geometry of quantum systems based on observed data, aiming to enhance the accuracy of quantum simulations and diminish computational costs. This algorithm leverages quantum geometry techniques to dynamically modify the system's topology, optimizing for specific simulation goals. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop utilizing the observed data to iteratively refine the quantum system's geometry, leading to improved simulation results. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, particularly in dynamically adapting to complex system dynamics.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum circuit design, termed Adaptive Self-Organizing Quantum Circuit Design. The core of this design centers on a dynamically adjusting circuit structure and parameters through an adaptive algorithm. Traditional circuit design relies heavily on manual adjustments, often requiring iterative refinement. Our method leverages self-organizing principles to automatically optimize circuit parameters based on predefined performance goals. The system's architecture is designed to be adaptable and robust, offering a significant advancement in automated quantum circuit construction.

title: 基于自组织网络的量子态控制
abstract: Quantum state control is a critical challenge in quantum computing, demanding precise manipulation of quantum states. Traditional approaches often rely on complex, pre-defined control sequences. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing self-organizing networks to dynamically adjust and control quantum states, offering a significant improvement in accuracy and efficiency. We propose a system based on establishing a dynamic network topology that allows for continuous, self-controlled state evolution. The core mechanism leverages the intricate interplay of entanglement and topology to achieve this control, surpassing limitations of current methods. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced precision and efficiency in various quantum operations, paving the way for more robust and scalable quantum computing architectures.

title: Dimension Reduction of Non-Linear Matrix Operations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of a novel dimension-reduction technique utilizing quantum geometry and non-linear matrix operations. Traditional matrix operations suffer from computational bottlenecks, and dimensionality reduction offers significant efficiency gains. We propose a method that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to fundamentally alter the matrix multiplication process, leading to exponential acceleration. The core mechanism involves translating matrix operations into quantum states, effectively utilizing quantum mechanics to enhance computational speed. We detail the theoretical framework and preliminary implementation of this technique, demonstrating its ability to achieve substantial improvements in matrix multiplication speed compared to standard algorithms. This research presents a promising avenue for enhancing computational capabilities, particularly in areas requiring massive matrix computations.

title: ZC-Edge Reproducibility Artifact: Executable Relying-Party Assurance Specification for Zero Trust Authorization and Attestation-Gated Secret Release
abstract: Reproducibility materials for the manuscript “ZC-Edge: An Executable Relying-Party Assurance Specification for Zero Trust Authorization and Attestation-Gated Secret Release.” The deposit contains the executable reference implementation, 13 unit tests, the 100-case requirement-derived conformance catalogue, five benign controls, fixed profile mappings, the evidence workbook, recorded result files, environment and build information, a bounded formal-analysis scaffold, editable figure sources, and integrity hashes. The 100 adverse cases were constructed by the authors from requirements R1-R10, with ten cases per requirement. They are not an expert-labelled or machine-learning dataset. The files support traceability, specification-conformance, implementation-fidelity, and local regression checks reported in the manuscript. They do not constitute production deployment evidence, a representative sample of real-world attacks, or an end-to-end confidential-computing performance benchmark.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Model with Adaptive Ensemble Representation
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian model designed to enhance predictive power and reduce variance by dynamically adjusting the ensemble of models. The model incorporates a mechanism for ensemble membership function adaptation, based on the inherent complexity of the input data. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional hierarchical models that rely on fixed ensemble structures. The core claim is that this enhanced model will achieve superior predictive accuracy and variance reduction through a novel, dynamically responsive ensemble. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulation studies and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance.
